Why does iOS ask for full calendar access?

Apple requires full calendar permission for an app to read events. Boarding Time uses that permission to display your calendars and does not create, edit or delete events.

What if I declined calendar access?

Open iOS or iPadOS Settings, find Boarding Time’s calendar permission and allow full access if you want to use the board. You can also use the Settings action shown by the app when access is denied. Return to the app to refresh.

Why is an event missing?

Check that the event exists in Apple Calendar, that Boarding Time has calendar access, and that the correct date and calendar are selected. In Settings → Lines, check the calendar is enabled; also check the board’s calendar filters. Calendar-provider synchronisation is managed by iOS and your provider.

Can I edit an event here?

Boarding Time does not edit events. Make changes in Apple Calendar or your usual calendar app. The native event viewer opened from Boarding Time has editing disabled.

Does it work on iPad?

Yes. The adaptive splash has been physically accepted in portrait, landscape and during rotation, with iPad calendar use and iPhone regression checks.

How do I remove local settings?

Revoking calendar access stops future access when the app rechecks permission, but does not erase saved calendar configuration. There is currently no erase-all control. Deleting the app removes its local app container; offloading preserves app data. System calendars, existing backups and information you have emailed are separate.

What should I include in a support email?

Include the app version/build, iPhone or iPad model, system version and steps to reproduce the issue. Please redact event titles, calendar names, notes and personal details from screenshots. Do not send passwords or unnecessary sensitive information.

Support is optional. Emails and attachments are handled separately from calendar data processed in the app. Read how support information is used.
